doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Composing away from the piano
summary: Carter calls the piano a crutch and works at the kitchen table.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: While we’re on this subject of composing, maybe we can go off on another tangent and just . . . you said that you prefer often not to write at the piano. Why is that?

Well, it’s because the piano to me is really a crutch. I hear more things away from the piano than I do at the piano. I guess at the piano you can sit and you’ll be doing one thing that you’re getting ready for tomorrow or the next day, and all of a sudden you’re wandering off into something else that you’re creating, you know. But if I get into a real bind, then I go to the kitchen table or the dining room table and as far away from the piano as I can.
